claims.text: Applicants must live in a low-income household.
Applicants must be ordinarily resident in Scotland at the time of applying.
Applicants must be entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK.
Applicants must not be eligible for public funds (e.g., grants or loans) towards the cost of tuition fees.
Applicants must not have already graduated with a university degree.
Applicants must have an unconditional offer for, or be a continuing student on, a full-time, part-time, or distance learning undergraduate degree course in academic year 2026-27.
The eligible institutions for undergraduate degrees include specific universities in Scotland, the Glasgow School of Art, the Royal Conservatoire of Scotland, and Scotland’s Rural College (SRUC).

Alternatively, applicants can have an unconditional offer for, or be a continuing student on, an undergraduate degree course validated by one of the listed Scottish universities but delivered at a different institution located in Scotland.
The application portal will be open from June 1, 2026, to 5 pm on December 1, 2026.
The grants cover the cost of tuition fees, up to £1,820 per year for a full-time degree course.
The purpose of the grants is to help students who do not have the financial resources to attend university.
Applications are made online.
Applicants must complete an eligibility checker before applying.
Applicants will receive an automatic reply confirming receipt of their application.
Applicants will be notified of the outcome of their applications within two to three weeks, provided all requested information and a timely referee response are received.
Retrospective applications will not be accepted.
CEF will not accept an application if the student has incurred tuition fee debts in a previous year of study and is unable to move to the next level of their course as a result.
Applicants eligible for a SAAS/Student Loans Company maintenance loan are expected to take full advantage of the loans available to them.

CEF will not consider an application if you are eligible for support (including loans) from Student Finance England, Wales or Northern Ireland, or any loan or grant from an overseas government or agency.
In general, CEF will not fund more than one repeat year for the same course and student.
If you previously received funding from the Carnegie Education Fund for an undergraduate degree and now wish to start a different course, your application may not be considered.

If you are a part-time student in receipt of tuition fee support from SAAS and are not eligible for any other grants, bursaries or loans, you may apply if the amount awarded by SAAS is less than the total amount of fees payable.
If you came to Scotland to study at university or college but have no experience of education in Scotland before that, and have no other ties to Scotland, you will not be considered eligible.
Applications from students who already have a university degree level qualification may be considered exceptionally at the discretion of CEF.

The Carnegie Education Fund has set aside a budget to fund students who completed an undergraduate degree in the past and wish to start an undergraduate degree in a different field of study in academic year 2026-27.
Students who have already started a 2nd degree before academic year 2026-27 are not eligible to apply.
The awards cover tuition fees only, up to a maximum of £1,820.
When assessing applications, the total household gross income thresholds are employed as guides, not hard cut-offs.
Applications are reviewed holistically, considering personal and financial circumstances.
If employed, gross pay (wages before deductions) is used for income assessment.
The student living cost loan or any social benefits (e.g., Universal Credit) are not regarded as part of an applicant’s total household income.
CEF may request additional supporting evidence.
In 2025-26, the median household income of award-holders was £10,000 per year.
Applications are considered on a case-by-case basis, taking into account household income and other extenuating circumstances.
The application portal is only accessible during the application window.

Late applications after the closing date will not be accepted, unless the student can demonstrate they were first informed that SAAS would not be covering their fees after CEF’s online portal has closed.
Supporting documents can be submitted as scanned copies or mobile images.
There is a 5MB size limit on each file submitted online.

Applicants must be ordinarily resident in Scotland at the time of applying and have completed at least two full years of secondary schooling or college education in Scotland, OR be able to demonstrate a substantial and recent connection to Scotland.
Applicants must be entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK, OR have Limited Leave to Remain valid for the entire duration of the course, OR be an asylum seeker.
The definition of 'ordinarily resident' used by CEF is the same as that used by the Student Awards Agency Scotland (SAAS).
To be considered ordinarily resident in Scotland, a person must have made their home in Scotland intending to stay and live there; being in Scotland solely to study does not qualify.

The following courses are not eligible for support: HNC and HND diploma courses, Access courses, Accelerated degree courses with a graduate entry, Courses delivered by or at a university outside Scotland, Courses at a Scottish Higher Education Institute delivered and validated by a university outside Scotland, Open University courses, Continuing Professional Development (CPD) courses, University courses below degree level, and Postgraduate degrees.
CEF will consider applications from students who meet the general eligibility criteria and have completed their first degree at least two years before the start of their new course.
Students applying for a second degree must enter the first year of their course in academic year 2026-27.
Students applying for a second degree must have been unable to gain employment in the subject area of their previous degree, be unemployed, have been made redundant, or be facing redundancy.

Students applying for a second degree must wish to reskill in a different field of study, unrelated to their previous qualifications, and recognised as being in a skills shortage area for the Scottish economy.

Eligible undergraduate degree courses for second degree applicants are listed by subject area, including Medicine and health, Social work, IT & Computing, Engineering and architecture, Quantitative sciences, Geosciences, Biosciences, and Cultural and creative studies.

CEF will take into account previous qualifications, length of time since previous qualification was obtained, current circumstances, and motivations for returning to university when considering applications for second degrees.
Applications will be processed on a first come first served basis.
No exceptions or exemptions will be made to any of the eligibility criteria.
The median household income of award-holders in 2025-26 was £10,000 per year.

Applicants must provide evidence of applicant eligibility, a letter of acceptance for their university course (or evidence of enrollment if a returning student), a SAAS Award Notice letter, and P60 or pay slips/Universal Credit statements.
Students receiving a SAAS bursary must also provide a copy of their SAAS award letter.
